title: Those given much are bound by covenant to seek others’ good
setting: Joseph Smith traveled to Missouri in April 1832 with Sidney Rigdon, Newel K. Whitney, and Jesse Gause. On 26 April a council of high priests and elders met in Independence. The council sustained Joseph as President of the High Priesthood. It also settled a dispute between Sidney Rigdon and Edward Partridge. Joseph dictated this revelation that afternoon, renewing the March call to form the United Firm.
summary: The revelation first tells the men that as they forgive each other, the Lord forgives them. It warns that all have sinned and that much is required of those given much. It says, “I, the Lord, am bound when ye do what I say,” but disobedience brings no promise. It names Edward Partridge, Newel K. Whitney, Sidney Gilbert, Sidney Rigdon, Joseph Smith, John Whitmer, Oliver Cowdery, W. W. Phelps, and Martin Harris. They are to be bound by a covenant in their stewardships over the poor and the bishopric. Their work covers both Zion and Kirtland, which the revelation calls a stake to Zion. Each has equal claims on the properties by just wants and needs, and surplus goes to the Lord’s storehouse. It ends with counsel to make friends with the “mammon of unrighteousness” and leave judgment to God.

contextNote.title: Why the warning comes with the forgiveness
contextNote.text: The council had just reconciled leaders who had offended each other. Verse 1 grants forgiveness, but verse 2 warns that all have sinned. Verse 3 explains the stricter standard: much given means much required. Verse 4 notes that these men had asked for and received many revelations. That “greater light” is why their sin brings “greater condemnation.” Verse 10 states the other side, that the Lord is bound when they obey. In this passage, accountability grows with what a person has been taught.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 81–83, “Much Is Given Much Is Required,” takes its title from verse 3. According to verses 17–19, what were members of the order to seek for their neighbors, and why?
reviewNote: Read all 24 verses. Heading gives Independence, 26 April 1832, the council, and Joseph being sustained as President of the High Priesthood. JSP historical introduction gives the Rigdon–Partridge reconciliation, the nine firm members, and Kirtland’s shifting status. The travel companions (Rigdon, Whitney, Gause) are from general history and JSP; JSP confirms Gause accompanied Joseph. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes. Setting checked against the official heading and JSP historical introduction.
